# Ontological Inventiveness

I sometimes wonder how I end up “leading” so many random weirdly shaped efforts. I don’t have the raw energy, resourcefulness, or charisma to operate the way I’ve seen highly effective traditional leaders do. I can’t handle wall-to-wall meetings like most execs seem to. Just two meetings in a single day can wipe me out. I spend most of my time and energy just laying around thinking, reading, and writing. This is not a leader-personality profile. But somehow I still manage to “lead” things. 

And while things I start don’t scale operationally or financially as much as traditionally led orgs do, they seem to scale well beyond personal or hobby scale. Before Summer of Protocols, I ran ribbonfarm as a fairly large multi-author blog for several years, and ran (or rather, instigated) Refactor Camp for nearly a decade. 

I think I’m able to “hack leadership” without having a leaderly personality due to 4 factors. 

* First, I use emerging technology aggressively. This reliably either lowers the burden of leadership to do a thing, and/or makes certain leadership functions unnecessary.

* Second, I tend to have very loose goals, good-enough standards, and no interest in either control or credit, which allows me to easily co-opt what others are doing anyway. I’m very easy to align with.

* Third, I rely a lot on getting people interested in *ideas* which can be viewed as parlaying *thought* leadership into *regular* leadership. This restricts the kinds of things I can lead to idea-centric ones, but in those domains it works better than people realize. 

* And finally, fourth (and this might be my main unusual trait), I think I have an eye for structuring things in weird or novel ways that make them much easier, and more importantly, personally fun to do.

This last trait is actually similar to being good at coming up with new named concepts and memes that shape, containerize, and label unusual patterns. Or porting org-structuring concepts from one domain to another. It’s a writing type skill, not a leadership type skill. Which is also why it’s good fodder for consulting.

I like to think of this as *ontological inventiveness* — the art of making up good, legible containers for squishy things. It’s like architecture or UX instincts and taste applied to activities rather than buildings.

To snowclone Alan Kay’s line: Ontological inventiveness is worth 80 leadership quotient points.
